cues.narration: Start a new fabric costing. Name the fabric, enter its warp and weft construction, and include the crimp and waste allowances.
Add the warp yarn's denier, beam ends, rate and G S T. These inputs determine warp consumption and cost.
Enter the weft denier, picks per inch, fabric width, yarn rate and G S T.
Review the weaving cost and overhead. Then enter your target margin and order quantity.
Now check Live Cost to review your estimate.
The production cost is thirty two rupees and eight paisa per metre.

cues.visual_anchor: Pricing assumptions and return to inputs
cues.narration: Review the pricing assumptions, then return to the inputs to explore a different costing scenario.

cues.visual_anchor: Change weft rate to ₹128/kg and margin to 15%
cues.narration: Increase the weft rate to one hundred and twenty eight rupees per kilogram, and set the margin to fifteen percent.

cues.visual_anchor: Reopen Live cost with changed inputs
cues.narration: Check Live Cost again to see the updated production cost and selling price.
Switch to Detailed to inspect the yarn calculations, including consumption, crimp and waste.
Scroll down to review the production cost breakdown. Quick and Detailed use the same calculations, with different levels of detail.
Save the quality and create its first costing together.
Review the assumptions, then save a reusable recipe and a fixed costing snapshot.

cues.visual_anchor: Search saved-quality library; open rate editor
cues.narration: Find the fabric in Saved Qualities. Open its rate editor to review the current yarn prices.
Change the warp rate to one hundred and thirty rupees per kilogram. Review the cost impact, then save and apply.

cues.visual_anchor: Select saved quality and restore inputs
cues.narration: Select the saved fabric again to restore its construction and costing inputs, without entering everything from scratch.

cues.visual_anchor: Find demo yarns; inspect linked quality
cues.narration: Find the demo yarns in Rate Book, and check which saved quality uses them.

cues.visual_anchor: Edit weft price and source note
cues.narration: Update the weft rate to one hundred and forty rupees per kilogram. Add a supplier note so you can identify the source.
Save the new rate, then open Activity to review the recorded change and its history.

cues.visual_anchor: Reopen saved quality and inspect its updated weft rate
cues.narration: Reopen the linked saved quality. Its weft rate reflects the Rate Book update, ready for your next estimate.

cues.visual_anchor: Apply quality, inspect inputs, open Live cost
cues.narration: Apply the quality and check its yarn inputs. Open Live Cost to review the recalculated production cost and selling price.

cues.visual_anchor: Find and open the earlier saved costing
cues.narration: Now open an earlier saved costing to compare it with the updated estimate.
The earlier costing keeps its original figures. Changing Rate Book does not rewrite saved costing snapshots.

cues.visual_anchor: Search for demo fabric and open its costing
cues.narration: Search for the fabric and open its saved costing to inspect the original figures.

cues.visual_anchor: Saved breakdown: cost, price, margin, quantity
cues.narration: This snapshot preserves the original inputs and results, so you can refer back to them.

cues.visual_anchor: Use snapshot; change weaving rate to ₹16/m
cues.narration: Choose Use to restore the inputs. Change the weaving rate to sixteen rupees per metre.

cues.visual_anchor: Set margin to 20%; open Live cost
cues.narration: Set the target margin to twenty percent, then open Live Cost to review the updated result.
Choose Save New Version. Version two preserves your changes while version one keeps its original figures.

cues.visual_anchor: Enable Compare and open version history
cues.narration: Enable Compare, then open the fabric's version history to choose the estimates.
Select versions one and two. You can now compare how the changed assumptions affect the same fabric.

cues.visual_anchor: Compare Costings: component and price differences
cues.narration: Open Compare Costings. Review the differences in production cost, selling price, margin and profit to understand the effect of your changes.

cues.visual_anchor: Internal cost-sheet export; business name and notes
cues.narration: For an internal record, enter your business name and notes, then download the detailed cost sheet.

cues.visual_anchor: Switch to Customer Quotation; buyer and terms
cues.narration: Switch to Customer Quotation. Add the buyer's name and your quotation terms, including delivery details.
Download the customer version. It includes the quotation details while keeping your internal costs and margins private.
Start by adding a production machine. Name it Demo Loom Zero One, and select Rapier as the machine type.
Add the machine. Your new loom is ready for assignment.

cues.visual_anchor: Add worker: Demo Operator 01, piece rate
cues.narration: Next, add Demo Operator Zero One. Select piece rate for this worker's pay type.

cues.visual_anchor: Role, approved operator, day availability, save
cues.narration: Set the role, keep the worker approved as a loom operator, and choose day availability. Then save the worker.

cues.visual_anchor: Activate Quality; choose saved costing v2
cues.narration: Activate a quality for production, and choose version two of the saved demo fabric.
Before production can start, check the required yarn stock. This fabric needs both warp and weft.

cues.visual_anchor: Add warp stock: 200 kg and note
cues.narration: Add two hundred kilograms of warp yarn, with a short stock note, then save.

cues.visual_anchor: Add weft stock: 200 kg and note
cues.narration: Repeat for the weft yarn. Add two hundred kilograms and a reference note, then save the stock.

cues.visual_anchor: Activate quality after stock is available
cues.narration: With both yarn stocks available, activate the quality for production.
Open Assign Looms for the active quality. Select Demo Loom Zero One and confirm the assignment.

cues.visual_anchor: Machine board; search for demo loom
cues.narration: The machine board connects your fabric to its loom. Search for the demo loom to find it quickly.
Open Manage Workers on the demo loom, and select Day Shift.

cues.visual_anchor: Search and assign Demo Operator 01; Done
cues.narration: Find Demo Operator Zero One, assign the worker, and finish setup. The loom now has a quality and a day operator.
Open the daily sheet for the correct date and shift. Enter two hundred and forty metres for the demo loom.
Open Worker Review to check output and earnings, then return to the sheet.

cues.visual_anchor: Save shift and confirm incomplete shift
cues.narration: Save the shift. Other machines remain pending, so only the demo loom has recorded output in this example.
Open the saved receipt to review the production record, including the loom, quality, operator and metres.
Two hundred and forty metres at sixteen rupees per metre gives earnings of three thousand eight hundred and forty rupees.

cues.visual_anchor: Find Demo Operator 01; production earnings card
cues.narration: Find Demo Operator Zero One to review the earnings generated from saved production.
Add an advance of four hundred rupees, with a short description, and save it.
The advance appears under Recovery, and the worker's net pay updates automatically.
You can also record a deduction. Select Other as the reason for this demonstration.
Enter fifty rupees.
Add a short note, then record the deduction.
Net pay is now three thousand three hundred and ninety rupees, after both recoveries.
Open How Pay Is Calculated for a summary of piece rate earnings, salaries and advance recovery.
Choose Mark Paid, then confirm the payment.

cues.visual_anchor: Paid state; cash payment is a record only
cues.narration: This records a cash payment. It does not send money.

cues.visual_anchor: Payroll records; period and worker search
cues.narration: Open Payroll Records and find the demo worker for the pay period.

cues.visual_anchor: Expand worker payment and loom breakdown
cues.narration: Expand the payment to see which loom, costing, rate and production quantity generated those earnings.
Switch to the Machines view to summarize production and worker cost by loom.
Download the C S V for spreadsheet analysis, or the P D F for a shareable payroll report.
